mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as predictor of 20-day SPX returns remains below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window or average 20-day return in declining FEDFUNDS periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 5-day SPX return in UNRATE > 4.5% for 3 months periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or signal triggers in >40% of cases without negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and retail sales indicates broad-based consumer demand weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction term (HOUST and RSAFS both declining) fails to predict negative returns: average 20-day return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for interaction term < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105.0) with concurrent weak GDP growth (GDPC1 < 2.0% annualized), supply-demand mismatch triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high industrial production with weak GDP growth
failure_condition: Average 60-day SPX return in regime condition periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or signal fails to outperform baseline in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment above 200,000 per month signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS as predictor of 20-day SPX returns remains below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window or average 20-day return in PAYEMS > 200k periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger premature monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 5-day SPX return in CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or signal triggers in >40% of cases without negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and rise in unemployment rate indicates supply chain disruption and labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Interaction term (INDPRO declining and UNRATE rising) fails to predict negative returns: average 20-day return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC for interaction term < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high retail sales growth (RSAFS > 0.5% m/m) with declining housing starts (HOUST < 0.0% m/m), consumer spending shift away from durable goods triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high retail sales with declining housing starts
failure_condition: Average 60-day SPX return in regime condition periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or signal fails to outperform baseline in >60% of cases.
